watch_outs: This is the record's one demo session; the paper reports 23 sessions from six bats (the Methods of Forli et al. 2025), and the record holds no other.

The behavior runs from -107.4 to 5248.6 s and the spikes from -12.7 to 5255.2 s: 1 of the 38 flights in epochs['flight'] lies wholly outside the neural recording, so analyses use params['analysis_epochs'], the flights clipped to it.

71 of 289 units fire above 2 Hz on average (one over the mean interspike interval, after the 1 ms rule; the record's NP_Bat_Demo.m computes it before); the script sets such units aside as putative interneurons before its place analyses. All are kept here, with label None.

Positions are the authors' processed behavior, not raw tracking: the record's NP_Bat_Demo.m says 'Processing mainly includes smoothing of position and flight segmentation', and the Methods of Forli et al. 2025 that positions 'were preprocessed ... to obtain continuous and smooth 3D positional data'. Speeds and held-sample counts describe that processing as much as the tracking.

339 runs of 11 or more identical position samples (10 or more repeats of the sample before; 264247 repeats, 41.11% of samples, 2202.0 s in all, the longest 807.3 s). Positions are kept as stored. A held run is lost tracking if the tracker repeated its last fix, or the animal holding still; check before analysing stops (wells, ripples). No speed limit is stated for this dataset, so fast steps are not counted.

23454 tracked position samples of 641157 (3.66%) lie outside the declared environment (env.bin_at gives -1): tracking beyond the apparatus, or an environment placed or sized wrong; 3.6% of stopped (below 0.5 m/s) samples and 4.6% of moving samples are outside. They are kept as stored and fall in no bin.
6 of 289 units have no spikes in the analysed epochs (params['analysis_epochs']); they are kept, as the file lists them, and are units['fires_in_epochs'] False.

cells.grid_score.note:
NotImplementedError: batch_grid_scores() needs a regular 2D grid of rectangular cells, one width along each axis; this environment's RegularGrid layout has no 2D grid of rectangular cells.
Why: the autocorrelogram shifts the rate map one cell at a time along rows and columns, so each shift is one distance only when the cells along an axis share one width.
Fix: use spatial_autocorrelation_radial(env, firing_rate), which works on every layout; a radial profile does not test for sixfold symmetry

cells.border_score.note:
NotImplementedError: Wall geometry needs a 2-D environment; this one is 3-D.
Why: walls and cell edges are lines in a plane.
Fix: compute wall-based measures on a 2-D environment

behavior.laps.note:
InputError: detect_laps(method='auto') cannot tell whether this 3-D environment has a loop.
Why: a lap goes around a loop of the space: a cycle of a track graph, or a hole in a 2-D area. Only those two kinds of environment are read.
Fix: for back-and-forth runs on a linear track or arm, use detect_trials(env, times, positions, regions=[start, end]); to segment round trips against a template, pass method='reference' with reference_lap=, which reports each round trip's direction along the track as 'increasing' or 'decreasing'.

ValueError: A regular grid over these positions would have 8,994,640,980 bins in 3 dimension(s), and its bin centers would need 215,871,383,520 bytes, more than the 8 GiB limit.
Why: each column of positions is one spatial dimension, so a transposed array of shape (n_dims, n_samples) reads as one dimension per sample; a bin_size far smaller than the arena has the same effect.
Fix: pass positions with shape (n_samples, n_dims), for example positions.T, and check that bin_size is in the units of positions

InputError: Interval filtering excluded ALL trajectory intervals (active gate(s) max_gap=1.0, min_speed=0.5, epochs, samples out of bounds or at NaN positions).
Why: no sampling interval is left to analyse; rather than return a result in which occupancy is zero in every bin, the call refuses.
Fix: check that min_speed=0.5 is in the positions' length units per second; check that epochs overlap `times` (same clock, seconds); check that positions use the environment's coordinates.
